body: Can confirm that the bug is also in Quarkus 1.13.0.Final
I have the same issue do we have any workaround solution?
I'm going to check this out.

For the record, requesting `localhost:8080/hello/greet` throws NPE because there is no endpoint mapped at that URL in the reproducer, ergo no ResourceInfo can be produced.

Question is if this situation can be resolved better. Injection producer is not allowed to return `null` (which would allow us to hand the responsibility to check null over onto the ContainerResponseFilter implementation). Maybe return an "empty" ResourceInfo, or throw an IllegalStateException instead of NPE... In any case it's not supposed to be execution as usual.

I didn't check the other cases where the filter is not called yet.

Regarding `ContainerResponseFilter` not being triggered for certain methods - it depends on the return type and it is purposeful. If the method returns Multi, the response filters are not triggered because by the time a filter would be triggered, data may already be streamed to the client, so e.g. trying to set response headers at that stage won't work. (A response filter triggers after a method invocation.)

If you need a filter to be triggered also for methods returning a `Multi`, use a `ContainerRequestFilter` or a `ResteasyReactiveContainerRequestFilter`, which are triggered before a REST method invocation and are triggered for all methods regardless of return type.

I you have a use case that is not accomodated by above, please share.

Thanks for looking into this.

I kind of expected that the response filter would always be executed before serializing the response. It's supposed to be a filter after all and not just a simple callback, but if the current behavior is deemed correct then your suggested workarounds will probably do the trick.

I guess it makes sense that ResourceInfo is null when there is no endpoint.

I wouldn't say it's a callback. The order actions in current implementation is:

* request arrives,
* invoke *request* filters,
* invoke the REST method,
* for non-streaming methods - invoke *response* filters; for streaming methods, data can already go through.

Allowing developers to modify response via a ResponseFilter for streaming methods would create a false impression that a developer can manipulate the response in certain ways which he cannot. E.g. modify headers (which he cannot because headers may have already been sent), or work with payload (which he cannot because it may still be being produced, or no data may have been produced yet).

Different semantics / implementations can be contemplated of course, but use cases should first be presented and analyzed to figure out what would be the best approach to solve them.

Is there something that a request filter doesn't allow you to do?

The use-case is primarily to set custom headers in responses, streaming and non-streaming.
This can indeed be achieved through `ResteasyReactiveContainerRequestFilter.getServerRequestContext().serverResponse().addResponseHeader` and it's is by no means a blocking issue for me, but since it's not very intuitive to use a request filter to add something to the response and also because the filter semantics was different in streaming and non-streaming endpoints I figured the response filter probably wasn't working as intended.

Obviously there are some methods in ContainerResponseContext that will never not work in a streaming response, so I totally get that a response filter can not work 100% the same for streaming and non streaming responses.

issue.title: Avoid potential NPE `@Context ResourceInfo` is used

body:
@TomasHofman's analysis is spot on.

However RESTEasy Reactive should certainly not be throwing a NPE. https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/pull/19062 takes care of that
